notes: Play action off i_formation_power -- Power's pulling-guard/FB-lead look is sold entirely through Pass Block (OL and FB), never a real Run/Pulling Block. RB fakes the Power mesh at Moment 0, then either blocks a free rusher in the back-side A gap or releases to the Flat checkdown per the block-or-release rule; A_L is the gap the Center does not own, matching the six-man split every other I Formation concept on disk uses. FB sells the lead block and settles into real pass protection as a seventh body outside the protection scheme, the same shape i_formation_pa_dagger uses. X and Z both run the Slant-n-Go and are authored as a leverage group rather than a fixed order: they are two mirrored deep routes with no true primary, which is the case play_instance_data_format.md Section 3 names for the group. Y's Go clears the middle third over the top of both. The RB checkdown is gated at Pressure Tier 2, not the Tier 1 every other Play Action instance uses, and that one digit is what makes this a shot rather than a checkdown play: at Tier 1 the safety valve is always in the read list, the double move never has time to finish, and the play measured 56% of its targets to the RB at 6.1 air yards a completion. At Tier 2 it is 18% to the RB at 13.5 air yards -- a real shot with a live valve. Tier 3 goes further (17.4 air yards) and is rejected because it kills the checkdown outright at 1%, which throws away the block-or-release rule the play is authored around. No alert candidate: the two Double Posts, the other Long Pass concepts built on a mirrored pair of deep routes, carry none either, and measurement confirms one would be inert here -- the leverage group is already the first read, so promoting it to the front moves nothing (66.6% completions against 66.8%).
